notes.title: Hotfix 1.1.1
notes.notes: Fixes a vital issue where controls would not instantiate correctly and would cause the game to become unplayable.

notes.title: Speedrun and Accessibility Update - Version 1.1.0
notes.notes:
​This version of Visual Out contains an extra menu with options for aiding accessibility and speedrunning.
This updates adds options for:
[list]
    [*]Map Assist mode that adds placement and item markers to the pause menu map
    [*]Always-On HUD for people who prefer a more traditional UI experience
    [*]Invincibility Mode
    [*]Infinite Energy Mode
    [*]Manual Text Advance mode for people having trouble reading on-screen dialogue
    [*]On-Screen Timer
    [*]Cutscene Skip mode for speedruns
    [*]Seeded Glyph Rooms, making speedruns more consistent between runs
[/list]

notes.title: Explore a dying PC in offbeat Metroidvania Visual Out
notes.notes:
Visual Out, a 2D Metroidvania-style platformer from solo developer MadameBerry Games, may have finally figured what happens when a computer inevitably, inexplicably slows down and dies: a little green man goes bebopping around cyberspace fighting programs.  

"As a program defying your operating system's wishes, plunge into the depths of a dying computer," its Steam page reads. "Uncover the secrets behind the computer's - and its creator's - demise."

Apart from discovery, your goal is to defeat the bosses of the PC's four sectors. But to even make it to them, you'll have to unlock six different abilities which focus on manipulating power, like "Jammer, Current, Turret" and others. 

There's something unsettling about Visual Out's world. It uses an abstract mix of digital and natural themes to create a surreal place where butterflies and jellyfish float alongside glitches and code given form. The sector bosses look almost like germs, and there's a desolation to it all. "They deserted us," it says. "You're all that's left." 

That aside, I'm more worried about the operating system. It acts like some kind of overseer, its directives periodically cutting through the game's synthy electronic soundtrack. "You have no choice but to execute your program, don't you?" it asks. "I pity you," it says. 

Visual Out is dripping with sci-fi meta-narrative funk and sounds like a fun, minimalist spin on Metroidvanias. It's available on Steam and Itch for $10. If you're looking for a faster, decidedly more neon 2D romp through a PC, have a gander at Exception, where you play a program trying to save an old woman's computer from a virus. 

Thanks, Kotaku.

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3
notes.notes:
​Two updates in this patch:
[list]
    [*]Fixed a backtracking issue at the lower-right part of the map that could cause players to get stuck at a save point.
    [*]Map tweak to make a late-game powerup more intuitive and provide room for an associated tutorial on the powerup.
[/list]

I don't like making map changes post-release, so this will be the only one.  I just had a real problem with the way this upgrade was handled, and I wish I had handled this pre-release.  But it is what it is.  The fixes should have no effect on saved games and you should be able to progress as normal, but if you do encounter errors due to the update, please let me know.

I've also been trying to get Steam overlay working, and while it works on Windows, I'm having trouble on Mac and Linux.  I'm going to tinker with it for a few days, and then probably post a patch in the "Test" build branch.

notes.title: Hotfix for Soft Lock and Title Screen Issues
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.2 includes the following hotfixes: 

[list]
    [*]Fixed a softlock with Boss 2
    [*]Fixed a softlock with Boss 4
    [*]Fixed hard-lock issue on the title screen for some users
    [*]Fixed exploit regarding Turret shields
    [*]Fixed issue where Turret shields appeared on enemies too early
    [*]Fixed collision in a save room
    [*]Added clarity to Boss 3 mechanics
[/list]

Thank you for your patience regarding these issues, and thank you to those who pointed them out for me.
